capabilities: render the live code a ledger block's decision governs, fetched from the repository at read time
report each decision's drift status: tracked, drifted by similarity percentage, or code gone
list every decision in the repository in a sidebar, worst first
re-check all decisions against current code with commands like Resolve all decisions
configure the ledger binary path and repository path, with a version check button
disambiguation: Not a decision-journal plugin; it binds existing decision notes to code in a git repository and reports staleness rather than helping you record decisions.
extras: Desktop-only (shells out to a local process, so it cannot work on Obsidian mobile). Requires installing the ledger binary, running ledger init in the repository, and configuring paths in settings. MIT licensed; the README notes this plugin reports drift but does not prevent it — the companion CI gate (ledger verify) does. The VS Code extension is named Decision Anchors because the Marketplace name was taken, but it is the same project.
motivation: The author built it because months after a decision is written down, the code has moved or been deleted while the note still confidently describes something that no longer exists, and nobody notices.
problem: Design-decision notes silently rot as the code they describe gets refactored or deleted, and nothing in Obsidian checks whether a note still matches its code.

relations.evidence: The plugin is a front end for ledger, a small Go binary that does the git work.
VS Code — Decision Anchors | code → note | Reading unfamiliar code, ask which decision governs this line

requires.name: ledger Go binary and a git repository with full history

summary: Note-side front end for the ledger CLI that renders the code a decision governs inside the note and reports when that code has drifted.
